authors: Brantly Callaway and Pedro H. C. Sant'Anna
title: Difference-in-Differences with multiple time periods
relevance: Provides group-time average treatment effects and inference for staggered Difference-in-Differences with heterogeneous treatment timing and effects.
interpretive_boundary: The method still requires a defensible comparison group and an explicit parallel-trends assumption; its availability does not identify the present design.

title: Estimating dynamic treatment effects in event studies with heterogeneous treatment effects
relevance: Shows how conventional two-way fixed-effect event-study coefficients can be contaminated under staggered timing and heterogeneous effects.
interpretive_boundary: The proposed estimator addresses heterogeneous timing, not invalid donors, spillovers, treatment ambiguity or destination-scope error.

authors: Michael G. Hudgens and M. Elizabeth Halloran
title: Toward Causal Inference With Interference
journal: Journal of the American Statistical Association
relevance: Formalises direct, indirect, total and overall causal effects when treatment can affect other units within groups.
interpretive_boundary: Its estimands and unbiased estimators rely on a specified grouped-interference setting and experimental assignment; the thesis uses it to motivate the spillover threat, not to estimate those effects.

title: Silhouettes: A graphical aid to the interpretation and validation of cluster analysis
journal: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
relevance: Defines the silhouette display and average silhouette width used to assess cluster tightness and separation.
interpretive_boundary: Silhouette quality evaluates geometry in the selected feature space; it does not validate commercial destination identities or causal relevance.

title: Comparing partitions
relevance: Provides chance-corrected partition-comparison foundations used for adjusted Rand stability diagnostics.
interpretive_boundary: Partition agreement measures stability relative to another partition; it does not establish that either partition is substantively correct.

title: Estimation and Inference of Heterogeneous Treatment Effects using Random Forests
journal: Journal of the American Statistical Association
relevance: Develops causal forests for heterogeneous treatment effects and inference under a potential-outcomes framework with unconfoundedness.
interpretive_boundary: The theoretical guarantees do not replace treatment identification, unconfoundedness, overlap or adequate effective sample size.

authors: Sören R. Künzel, Jasjeet S. Sekhon, Peter J. Bickel and Bin Yu
title: Metalearners for estimating heterogeneous treatment effects using machine learning
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
relevance: Organises supervised learners into S-, T-, X- and related strategies for estimating conditional average treatment effects.
interpretive_boundary: Flexible outcome learning does not by itself justify a causal estimand, remove confounding or create stable heterogeneity information from a very small treated sample.
